newsitem.title: INDIA: Internet sites celebrate India's golden jubilee. [CORRECTED 11:28 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Internet sites celebrate India's golden jubilee. [CORRECTED 11:28 GMT]

text.p: India's Internet champions are marking the country's 50th anniversary of independence from British rule by launching World Wide Web sites celebrating its culture and achievements.

"There is no sponsor, but we had to create it as a gift to the nation on the 50th anniversary," Aslam Shems (corrects from Salaam Shems), president of Delhi-based Combit Advertising Network Ltd, an Internet advertising company, told Reuters on Tuesday.
Combit's website, whose address is www.iloveindia.com, will be officially launched at midnight of August 15, exactly 50 years after the moment of independence, Shems said.
But the site is already open with a potpourri aimed at a worldwide Indian diaspora.
Shems said net-surfers can listen to 100 songs from 50 years of movie music at a virtual jukebox and view at least 600 images of modern India, including rare independence pictures.
They can also join a bulletin board to discuss good, bad and ugly issues related to India.
Shems said corruption in Indian politics was a favourite topic of conversation.
A song titled "I love you India," has been specially recorded for the site.
"We have got all images, not just cows and monkeys," Shems said, referring to what he said were stereotyped images of India.
The country offers many modern sounds, images and achievements, he said.
The site also includes a travel planner on India, and is expected to serve as a site for India lovers long after the anniversary is over, Shems said.
Another company, MediaWeb, has launched a website with the address www.india50.com.
According to Web Vision magazine, this will highlight the achievements of Indian companies.
A Britain-based website, www.india50.co.uk, aims to list events marking the golden jubilee celebrations of Indian independence.
Independent Internet lovers have also contributed to other sites marking the anniversary.
